items.title: QAMM: Adjoint MeanFlow Matching for Few-Step Offline Reinforcement Learning
items.abstract: Flow policies can model rich action distributions, but their iterative sampling limits decision speed. Adjoint matching uses the critic's action gradient to improve a flow policy without backpropagating through its sampling trajectory, yet its supervision is defined for instantaneous velocities. We propose QAMM, a method that turns the critic-derived adjoint signal into supervision for MeanFlow's average velocity. The resulting policy learns finite-interval transport directly and generates actions with few network evaluations. We derive the adjoint MeanFlow target, specify its gradient boundaries, and train it with an offline actor-critic. On ten HumanoidMaze tasks, QAMM produces effective two-call policies and achieves competitive performance against strong flow-policy baselines. These results show that adjoint-based Q optimization can be combined with average-velocity learning to obtain expressive offline policies with few-step action generation.

items.llm_tldr_en: Flow policies model rich action distributions but their iterative sampling slows decisions. QAMM converts the critic-derived adjoint signal into supervision for MeanFlow average velocity, yielding few-step policies trained with an offline actor-critic that perform competitively on ten HumanoidMaze tasks.
items.llm_tldr_cn: 流策略能刻画丰富的动作分布，但迭代采样导致决策速度受限。伴随匹配利用评论家的动作梯度改进流策略而无需对采样轨迹反向传播，但其监督仅定义在瞬时速度上。QAMM 将评论家导出的伴随信号转化为 MeanFlow 平均速度的监督，使策略直接学习有限区间传输并以少量网络评估生成动作，并在十个 HumanoidMaze 任务上取得具竞争力的少步策略性能。
